description: Cavalry traditions varied widely but were often central to warfare, scouting, raiding, and elite status. Steppe peoples such as the Scythians, Sarmatians, and Xiongnu emphasized highly mobile horse archers and fast-moving mounted warfare, while Persians, Macedonians, Seleucids, and other Hellenistic states fielded powerful shock cavalry and heavily armored horsemen. Celtic, Iberian, Germanic, and Numidian societies also developed distinctive mounted traditions suited to local terrain and tactics, from swift javelin cavalry to noble warrior horsemen. Together, these cultures made cavalry one of the ancient world’s most flexible and prestigious military arms, valued for speed, maneuver, pursuit, reconnaissance, and decisive battlefield charges.
